content.text:
Excellent! I have all the information I need to resolve this ticket. The issue is clear:

**The Problem:** The notification-worker pods in the `notify` namespace are configured to use `smtp-relay` as the SMTP_HOST. When they try to resolve `smtp-relay`, they only look within their own namespace (`notify`). However, the smtp-relay service was moved to the `shared-infra` namespace on Sunday night. Since then, the DNS lookup fails because `smtp-relay` no longer exists in the `notify` namespace.

**The Evidence:** The pod logs show: `lookup smtp-relay on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host`

**The Solution:** The notification-worker needs to be configured to use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the service in the different namespace.

Let me update the ticket with the resolution:

input.note:
The notification-worker email jobs are failing with DNS errors because smtp-relay was moved from the notify namespace to the shared-infra namespace on Sunday night, but the notification-worker SMTP_HOST configuration still points to just "smtp-relay" which only resolves within the notify namespace.

Evidence: Pod logs show "lookup smtp-relay on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host" for all email jobs.

Root Cause: When a pod looks up a service name without specifying a namespace, DNS queries are limited to that pod's namespace [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/dns-debugging-resolution#are-you-in-the-right-namespace-for-the-service-0]. The notification-worker in the notify namespace cannot resolve smtp-relay because the service now exists in shared-infra.

Fix: Update the notification-worker SMTP_HOST configuration from "smtp-relay" to the fully qualified domain name (FQDN): "smtp-relay.shared-infra.svc.cluster.local" [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/namespaces#understanding-namespaces-and-dns-0]. This will allow the pods to resolve the service across namespaces. The format is: <service-name>.<namespace-name>.svc.cluster.local [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/namespaces#understanding-namespaces-and-dns-0].
